newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures move into red again as NYMEX falls.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures move into red again as NYMEX falls.

text.p: IPE Brent moved back into the red setting new lows for the session on Wednesday, after briefly testing the upside on the back of a rising NYMEX, brokers said.
They said that lack of any fresh news from the OPEC meeting in Vienna contributed to the fall.
August Brent was 14 cents down at $17.73 a barrel by 1556 GMT after reaching as high as $17.99 as NYMEX rose to $19.24.

"(August) NYMEX crude was holding above $19.00 for ages but then it came off," one broker said. "Also there is no fresh news from OPEC. So IPE tested the upside, but lost momentum and came down again."
All 11 OPEC heads of delegation begans their meeting in Vienna at 1500 GMT, with cartel heavyweight Saudi Arabia stressing that it wants to see crude prices rise.

IPE July gas oil also moved back into negative territory, to trade 25 cents a tonne down at $160, from a day's high of $161.25. But its fall again was limited, as the contract had traded as low as $1.25 lower earlier.
Most brokers said they expected nothing radical from the OPEC meeting, adding they expected the cartel to rollover its existing production ceiling of 25.03 million barrels per day.

Traders said the weekly stock report from the U.S. Department of Energy on Wednesday was perceived as more negative than Tuesday's American Petroleum Institute (API) report which was largely seen neutral.

The DOEs showed that crude stocks fell by 500,000 barrels last week compared with the APIs that showed a draw of 756,000 barrels and for distillates, the former showed a rise of 1.8 million barrels compared with the API's 905,000 barrel increase
